theorem: Let rho1,rho2 be arbitrary PPT states on A_i tensor B_i with dim(B_i)<=3, and let K_i:A_i->C^2 be arbitrary linear maps. Regroup the tensor product across (A1 A2):(B1 B2). After the local filter K1 tensor K2 on Alice, the result is separable across the regrouped bipartition. Any subsequent local linear map on either composite party, including an arbitrary nonfactorized Bob 9->4 map and any invertible Alice output filter, preserves separability. In particular this applies to two arbitrary 3x3 PPT states. The analogous statement holds with Alice and Bob exchanged. This elementary deduction imports the 2x2/2x3 PPT-separability theorem and is not claimed novel.
named_import_and_proof: Michal, Pawel and Ryszard Horodecki, https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9605038, show PPT is necessary and sufficient for separability in 2x2 and 2x3. Each (K_i tensor I)rho_i(K_i tensor I)^* is PPT by local congruence, and its supports have dimensions at most 2 and 3, so it is separable by that theorem (a zero component gives the trivial zero output). Writing each as a positive sum of product projectors and tensoring yields a positive sum of projectors onto (a1 tensor a2) tensor (b1 tensor b2). Any subsequent local map sends such a product projector to another product projector. The same argument applies termwise to any finite nonnegative mixture of products of such PPT inputs.
crosshatch_coordinate_corollary: For the trace64 Q tensor Q source in frontier-20261028-crosshatch-coordinate-sn2-v1.json SHA256 9071fcc25e96f25e4e6dd96ba38403407fb86fc83e00898687114a700f061d8f, nine of the 126 four-coordinate subsets of either 9-dimensional local space have the Cartesian form S1 x S2, |S1|=|S2|=2. The corresponding rank-four filter factors as the tensor of two coordinate rank-two filters. Hence if either side uses one of those nine subsets, the 4x4 output is separable even for an arbitrary map on the opposite party. Among the 15876 simultaneous coordinate cuts, at least 9*126+126*9-9^2=2187 are therefore separable. This is a lower bound; no exact count of separable cuts is claimed.
explicit_one_copy_checks: For Q's six individual 3x3 coordinate row/column deletions, the checker gives elementary 3- or 4-phase product decompositions without importing the Horodecki theorem: Alice deletions 0,1,2 use product factors (|1>+z|2>) tensor (|0>+z|2>), (|0>+z|2>) tensor (z|0>+|1>+z^-1|2>), and (|0>+z|1>) tensor (|0>+z|2>), with one residual product loop in the first and third cases. Bob deletions 0,1,2 use (|0>+z^-1|2>) tensor (|1>+z|2>), (|0>+z|1>+z^2|2>) tensor (|0>+z|2>), and (|0>+z^-1|2>) tensor (|0>+z|1>), again with one residual product loop in the first and third. Use z^3=1 for three-factor groups and z^4=1 for four-factor groups. These examples illustrate but do not substitute for the imported arbitrary-map theorem.

exact_check.observed: Exact Laurent-integer arithmetic checked all54 rank-one minor polynomials and all486 matrix entries for the six one-copy identities, and verified phase exponent separation. This is not a computational proof of 2x3 PPT separability; that result is explicitly imported.

limits: The factorized rank<=2 condition on one composite local filter is essential to this argument; a genuinely joint rank-four filter need not be covered. The result neither proves all 4x4 PPT states separable nor resolves the SN>=3 witness target. No novelty, formal proof, or independent external/human review is claimed.
